trap_recorded.summary: The battle struct at 0x020159E4 is scratch for ~10 s after a turn closes (count 7 -> 328201/328711 -> 7 again, roster tile already moved). A resume guard read inside that window fails the roster shape. Not a damaged battle and not a DE-028 desync: a 40 s read-only hold with no input left the roster perfect and the ROM byte-identical. The adopt now retries to a 45 s bound, records every attempt, and sends 'c' between attempts (a served read halts the core, so a read-only retry freezes the engine inside the transition - 16 identical scratch reads before the cont was added).

a5_2.scope: pure host contract only; no engine legality, menu acceptance or live wiring is claimed by this subpacket

criteria.expected: the frozen schema versions, precedence, selectors, reason codes and fallback semantics implemented exactly as frozen in docs/tactics-policy.md
criteria.observed: choose_action(snapshot, policy) -> decision | None and evaluate() -> outcome/reason/scope/rule_id/decision/detail implement the frozen contract; schema strings are ffta-tactics-policy/1 and ffta-tactics-snapshot/1; assignment precedence is character -> job -> party with first-match-wins and no cross-scope fall-through (a matched scope governs, its own fallback applies).

criteria.expected: every supported rule evaluated, threshold boundaries exact, absent facts making a rule ineligible rather than permissive
criteria.observed: relation/kind/action_id/ability_name, actor and target HP percent (floored integer percent; lte 25 includes exactly 25 while lt 25 excludes it), remaining MP after cost at the exact 0 and 1 boundaries, and actor/target status present/absent over the frozen byte vocabulary are all exercised; a missing HP/MP/status fact rejects the predicate (an absent status block is NOT 'known absent').

criteria.expected: unknown keys and invalid thresholds rejected at load; missing legality or actor identity means no commit
criteria.observed: ~40 rejection cases pass: unknown keys at every level, wrong schema, unknown fallback/selector/relation/kind/party key/status name (case-sensitive)/comparison operator, ~10 malformed threshold shapes, malformed character/job/party keys, duplicate rule id. Runtime fail-closed cases pass too: identity other than verified, snapshot older than max_age_seconds, malformed snapshots (duplicate candidate ids, bad stats/tiles/status bytes, unknown keys), zero/absent candidate facts and engine-illegal (legal=false) candidates are never selectable, including as the Wait fallback.

limitations: Pure host control-flow evidence only: the suite cannot show that any candidate is engine-legal in the game or that a real menu accepts the chosen command.
No runner wiring yet: A5.3 proves the minimum conditional-action adapter and A5.4 integrates it live; A5.1's scenario Move/Wait assignment is unchanged.

Position/distance, reachability, damage or hit estimation, item counts, revive, law constraints, movement preference and multi-turn planning are unsupported and a policy using them fails to load rather than being ignored.
Status vocabulary covers the live +0xe8..+0xed named bits only; durations (+0xd9..+0xe7), +0xe8 bit 0 and the numeric +0xed bits 5-7 stay unexposed.
Candidate id canonical form is a documented adapter convention, not enforced by the loader; only uniqueness and the tie-break role are contractual.
Healer and resource-preservation presets are A6 (they need MP/item/recovery facts outside this freeze).

a5_3.scope: minimum conditional-action adapter, proven live for a deliberately narrow candidate family (engine-offered Move and Wait). Ability candidates, MP cost and range targeting are NOT proven and stay unsupported.

The adapter reads the two C2/C3 planners (plan_identified_move / plan_identified_wait) and emits exactly {move, wait} in id order; with a command byte outside 0/1/2 it emits no candidates and the chooser returns None with reason no-legal-candidate. A bad policy raises at adapter construction.

criteria.expected: an unsupported predicate cannot silently become an enabled option; unsupported controls are recorded as not applicable rather than as passing
criteria.observed: 94/94 host checks pass. The adapter supplies no MP cost, range, target or ability fact, so relation/target/ability predicates are ineligible and a policy naming an unknown status or unsupported key fails to LOAD. The packet's 'insufficient MP' and 'illegal range/target' controls are therefore not applicable to this family and are recorded as open for the ability family (docs/tactics-policy.md, 'Explicitly not proven by A5.3').

limitations: Narrow family: only the engine-offered Move and Wait are candidates. Ability candidates (command cursor 1 -> ability list -> target mode) are not decoded, so the 'insufficient MP' and 'illegal range/target' controls are not applicable here and remain open.

A Move candidate asserts that the menu offers the Move command, not that a destination is reachable; reachability is decided by the engine at the confirm and verified by the whole-party tile delta afterwards.

Stale-snapshot rejection is host-proven only; the live observations measured 1.5-1.6 s of age (dominated by the boundary screenshot) against the 5.0 s policy budget, so no live run happened to be stale.
Both live runs stopped on the turn budget (2 turns) as intended; this packet makes no complete-battle, defeat, takeover or resume claim (those remain A5.1/C3 evidence).
The live conditional family is a condition on the actor's own engine-read state (HP percent and which commands the menu offers), not on a target: the adapter exposes no target unit for a Move.

Mode label: run.json still records mode 'retail-ai' for the policy run (the field names the enemy-turn behaviour, which is unchanged); the policy path is named by tactics_policy and by each turn event's tactics record.

limitations: Verified seven/eight-record fixture scope; player side_bit false is fixture-specific.
The manual layer's parked-menu gate is evidence, not proof: the whole-board tile delta after the manual turn is the falsifier.
Fresh-menu cursor-own-tile law is not used to infer actors while targeting.
Scenario Move/Wait assignment is not a conditional tactics policy.
No multi-player end signature or complete-battle acceptance; both resumed legs stopped on the turn budget.
The resumed legs' turns were identified Waits in the canonical run (position_before still proves continuation); the repeat run shows Moves from the manual tile.
No ROM bytes or bulk memory dumps committed; raw local evidence (including the window PNGs) stays ignored and is cited by sha256.
The turn-transition scratch window (DE-032) is bounded to 45 s in the adopt; a much longer transition would still fail the guard honestly.
